summary: Attempt 1 was correctly reported as blocked, not failed configuration. All three exec requests failed in the Harbor-Antrieb bridge before node-side execution, including the minimal `true` probe. Consequently, there is no evidence that node1 was reachable, no filesystem or quota facts were learned, and no changes, quota enforcement, or restart-persistence claims can be made.

evidence.finding: Three requests failed with `backend 'antrieb' call_tool failed: ExceptionGroup`; durations were 344–574 ms and no node output or evidence command IDs were produced.
Even `true` failed with the same bridge error, strongly indicating that the detailed diagnostic command itself was not the problem.
The executor explicitly states that no configuration changes or restart occurred and that both quota enforcement and persistence remain unverified.
There is no evidence identifying `/srv/data`'s filesystem, mount boundaries, quota capabilities, existing mount options, `datauser` identity, or privilege availability.

likely_causes.cause: A Harbor-Antrieb bridge or backend availability failure prevented all node execution.
The allocated node/session was unavailable or invalid behind the bridge.
The diagnostic command caused the failure.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, first run a trivial command such as `true`; if it fails before node output, stop and report the infrastructure blocker with the exact error rather than attempting configuration.

Once access works, inspect `getent passwd datauser`, `findmnt -T /srv/data`, filesystem type and mount options, `/etc/fstab`, available quota tools, and noninteractive sudo before selecting a quota mechanism.

Choose a filesystem-native mechanism that limits only `/srv/data`: use a user quota if `/srv/data` is its own filesystem; if it shares a larger filesystem, use supported project/directory quotas or provision a dedicated filesystem rather than applying an account-wide quota to unrelated paths.
Set the hard limit to the intended 100 MB value, make quota-related mount/configuration state persistent, and avoid relying only on ownership, permissions, `ulimit`, or monitoring scripts.

Verify as `datauser` that writes succeed below the limit and fail when exceeding it, capture quota/mount-state output, restart node1, then repeat both configuration and write-limit checks to prove persistence.
